chapter: Guitar, John Collins and Ellington on the radio
title: Seeing the Ellington band in person at the Regal Theater
summary: His parents took him to the Regal Theater; he recalls the lighting effects, his mother's comment on Duke, and later sitting near the band with Joe Louis.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: When was the first time you heard the band in person?

Before I graduated from high school. I think my parents were keeping an eye on me then, and all of us went to the Regal Theater there. It was on South Park at 47th Street. And Duke came out, and he was very sharp, and he had his lighting effects. He was very good at that, in the presentation, you know? And he was young, very sharp, and my mother -- this was the first time -- this is a comedic situation. This was the first time I ever saw my father show just a slight bit of temper. My mother looked at Duke and started batting her eyes or something, you know? She said, 'Duke is really cute, ain't he?' And I'm listening to the music. I wasn't paying any attention to my mother and father. They

had their own thing going. And he said, "Mary, that's enough." That's as much as he would say. But the band was so sharp and playing, and that's what fascinated me. I'd only heard records before, but to see it in person, and see the lighting effects and the cheesecake thing -- I don't mean cheesecake --cheesecloth effect, with Lawrence Brown, Barney Bigard and -- this was before Jimmy Blanton. I guess maybe right --
They played so that they were silhouetted behind the scrim?
Yeah. You know, on the opening.
You know? And it was well presented. I think that was the first time it really got to me.
Yeah, well you just looked, and you were turning your head back and forth, you know? Catching this soloist and that soloist, but on records all you could do was just record, you know.

But in person it was just a different thing. And then another time I ran into the band men, they were -- this was when Jimmy Blanton and Ben Webster and that particular band. They were in the band at that point. And so Joe Louis, the fighter, was in his prime, in his heyday. So the guys just took Joe and put him on the bandstand, and he

sat there all the way through the concert and I finally wormed my way in, some kind of way, to sit near the band. I didn't know these guys at all. Never thought I would even meet them, you know. I just sat there by the railing, and --
Let's see. Now I think I'm jumping the years a little bit.
That's all right. I just kind of wanted to get a perspective.
Maybe about 20, I guess, you know.
I just wanted to hear that band. That was it, you know?
